minutes.headline: Task force skipped the spring Green Communities grant round and set an Aug 15 / Sept 15 / Oct 15 timeline for the fall round.
minutes.summary: The Green Community task force approved the May minutes, then explained why no spring grant application went in: the sewer pump projects had a long payback and would have cleared only a small amount. The group discussed building needs (windows here, Turkey Hill, library, town hall), set working deadlines for the fall application, and heard outreach and LED streetlight updates. A July 1 Zoom meeting was planned and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The task force skipped the spring Green Communities grant round, deciding to aim for the fall round instead.
The group set a working timeline for the fall application: a project list by Aug 15, finalized projects by Sept 15, and submission by Oct 15.
The chair will email departments and circulate the capital planning list to gather small projects that could be bundled into one application.
Members heard that LED streetlights have sharply cut the electricity bill compared with the old monthly bill, and agreed to keep up Facebook outreach.
A Zoom meeting was planned for Monday, July 1. No votes were taken beyond the minutes and adjournment.

why_it_matters: Green Communities grants can pay for energy projects in town buildings and vehicles, so the fall round is the next chance for such work to be funded by the state rather than by the local tax levy.

The packages discussed (pump stations, a police cruiser, windows, Turkey Hill, the library, Town Hall) are all capital items, so any that are applied for may later come to residents as funding requests.
